subject: Onboarding: model compatibility & traffic assumptions (context-window tradeoffs)
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Morgan <alice@osiris.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding: model compatibility & traffic assumptions (context-window tradeoffs)

Hi Alice / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. As promised, attaching our initial working assumptions so we can lock down the implementation scope for week 1. High-level asks below and a short recommended shortlist. Please review and flag anything that doesn't match your expectations.

Key asks from Osiris so far:
- Primary feature: long-form summarization + answer extraction from multi-document bundles (typical doc bundle size: 3–7 docs, ~15–30k characters).
- Latency target: 300–600ms P50 for API path; background async jobs can tolerate minutes.
- Expected steady-state traffic: 120k user-initiated requests/month, average 1.2k tokens/request (includes prompt + expected model response).
- Peak burst: 250 RPS sustained for ~5–10 minutes during scheduled jobs (midnight ET batch).

Initial recommendations (shortlist):
1) open-llm-xlarge-8k: lowest cost, 8k context. Good for early rollout (smaller KV cache, lower per-token cost). Expect ~P50 380ms on Dedicated-1 GPU.
2) open-llm-std-32k: supports the full doc bundle without pre-chunking. Higher VM requirements and ~1.6x token cost vs 8k variant.
3) redwood-qs-16k (quantized): middle ground, ~1.1x cost vs 8k, recommended for mixed load if you need some long context support without full 32k infrastructure.

Attached: token_profile_v1.xlsx (token distribution + hourly bands), context_examples.pdf (doc bundle samples).

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm true avg tokens/request (we used 1.2k as conservative).
- Agree on initial context strategy: start with 8k + client-side chunking OR target 16/32k model for a single-pass UX.
- Schedule a short am/pm ops call to validate burst routing and caching (30m).

If you confirm by Tue EOD we’ll draft the mutual action plan (MAP) and provision a staging workspace with the 8k variant and a fallback 16k image for canary.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: token_profile_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)]
[Attachment: context_examples.pdf (pdf, 220KB)]

From: Alice Morgan <alice@osiris.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@osiris.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding: model compatibility & traffic assumptions (context-window tradeoffs)

Hi Markus —

Thanks — this is a helpful starting point. A couple of clarifications from our side before we commit:

1) Token math: the 1.2k tokens/request seems low for our higher-detail summaries. Our internal telemetry for a 7-doc bundle shows median ~2.5k tokens when we include retrieval context. We can export a sample telemetry table if that helps.

2) Peak characteristics: those midnight jobs are actually two separate cron workers firing in parallel (we expect combined burst ~420 RPS for 7–9 minutes). Can you confirm the autoscaling behavior and whether that fits within your Dedicated burst capacity?

3) Compliance note: we’ll need evidence of data retention policies and the ability to run in a private VPC for any production rollout. I attached our standard compliance checklist.

Also, question on UX: if we pick the 8k path and do client-side chunking, will extractive fidelity suffer (where the model misses cross-chunk references)?

Thanks — will route a quick internal note to procurement once we have the MAP and a rough quote for the 3-month pilot.

Best,
Alice Morgan
Head of Product — Osiris AI
[Attachment: compliance_requirements.docx (docx, 92KB)]

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Morgan <alice@osiris.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding: model compatibility & traffic assumptions (context-window tradeoffs)

Hi Alice —

Quick answers inline + an updated recommendation: 

- Token estimate: If your telemetry shows median ~2.5k tokens/request that materially changes cost and routing. Please send the sample telemetry export and we’ll re-run cost sims.

- Burst capacity: Dedicated can provision a "burst pool" for predicted cron windows. For a combined 420 RPS spike we recommend configuring a short-lived autoscale ramp to add 2 extra Dedicated worker nodes for the batch window; that keeps P50 latency under 500ms for the 8k variant in our sims. I’ll add the autoscale policy to the MAP draft.

- Client-side chunking tradeoffs: cross-chunk context is the main risk. We recommend a progressive approach:
  * Phase 1 (pilot): 8k model + retrieval + dense overlap (200–300 token slide) for chunk boundaries. This keeps cost down and lets us measure extraction precision vs user-level gold.
  * Phase 2 (scale): if cross-chunk misses exceed your error threshold, move to redwood-qs-16k to reduce chunking or to 32k for single-pass processing.

Updated shortlist rationale:
- If median tokens/request = ~2.5k => recommend starting pilot on redwood-qs-16k to reduce engineering lift; 8k becomes cost-optimal only where you can enforce aggressive chunking and reconcile answers post-hoc.
- If median remains ~1.2k => 8k remains the clear starter option.

I'll re-run the per-token cost sim once you share telemetry. Also linking the MAP draft once Markus posts it.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: N/A]

From: Alice Morgan <alice@osiris.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@osiris.ai>, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding: model compatibility & traffic assumptions (context-window tradeoffs)

Markus / Priyom —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. We exported a 7-day sample telemetry file and sent it to your shared Drive link (Drive: Onboarding/OSR-token-profile). The median is ~2.4k tokens/request, 95th percentile ~6.8k.

Decision: we want the pilot to favor developer velocity and fidelity — please provision the redwood-qs-16k image for staging (canary) and also configure an 8k worker pool for cost-testing. We’re happy to start with the 16k image for UI flows and have 8k workers for background low-cost processing.

Please send the MAP and a pilot quote (3 months) and include the private-VPC option and evidence items for the compliance checklist. Also confirming the 30m ops call — Tue 2026-09-01 10:00AM ET works for our team.

Appreciate it —
Alice
Head of Product — Osiris AI
